brief:
What has been decided:

- The remote is for television only, not a universal multi-device remote, and targets younger users (under 40) rather than an older demographic (TS3012b: "I think we should go for universal, because apparently we're a separate company"; TS3012c: "We're definitely focussing on the younger people, 'cause that was our main goal.")
- The case will be rubber (chosen for durability against drops and because it suits the spongy, trend-researched feel the young target group wants), and the base colour will be yellow with black buttons (TS3012c: "Okay, so we're definitely going for rubber.")
- Both an LCD screen and speech recognition are included, putting the design on the "deluxe edition" path, with an advanced chip to support them (TS3012c: "I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want."; TS3012c: "The chip is advanced because we have the advanced features.")
- Energy source is regular (non-rechargeable) batteries (TS3012c: "energy, we choose regular regular batteries")
- A lost-remote locator (beep, paired with a simple LED) will be included (TS3012b: "the beep is a very simple thing to imple implement, just make a button on your T_V_ and just hit the button, it beeps somewhere.")
- A scroll-wheel was voted out after discussion (TS3012c: "Let's vote on it. Then we don't have to talk about it any longer. What do you want? In or out?"; TS3012c: "No r no scroll-wheel. Okay. Um I don't see anything missing really.")

What changed along the way:

- Meeting b's idea of a rechargeable battery with a docking station was dropped by meeting c in favour of plain regular batteries once the actual component list didn't include a rechargeable option (TS3012b: "Shall we uh also look if it's possible to make a rechargeable remote?"; TS3012c: "it wasn't it wasn't in the options, a rechargeable m module actually.")
- The LCD screen went from an early "let's cut it" lean to a firm "keep it" once marketing data showed the young target group wants it (TS3012b: "I think we should lose the L_C_D_ screen, like you said."; TS3012c: "I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want.")
- Speech recognition went the same way, from "too hard across multiple countries" to included once the component turned out to be small and cheap (TS3012b: "Speech recognition, I think it's very hard, because we're selling across multiple countries."; TS3012c: "So why why if it's small and we can imp why shouldn't we?")

Open actions and owners:

- No one yet has the actual finance/cost information needed to check the LCD + speech recognition + advanced chip + rubber combination against the ~12.50 Euro production target; the team explicitly went into their third meeting without it and decided to proceed on design merit alone rather than cost (TS3012c: "too bad we don't have any finance information apparently"; TS3012c: "so you just do whatever you like and uh doesn't care what it costs") -- getting real numbers before the final meeting should be the top priority.
- The team split further design and research work going into the final meeting: one member on market/trend analysis, the project manager on the year-end project report (TS3012c: "we're gonna work on our own because you're gonna do the market market uh analysing")

Disagreements still open:

- Whether to lean into a literal fruit/vegetable-inspired shape for the base design (not just as an optional cover) was raised but left unresolved: one member liked the fruit-shape idea, while another warned it's a seasonal trend risk for a core design choice, and the team provisionally sided with keeping fruit theming to optional covers only -- but this wasn't put to a final vote the way the scroll-wheel was (TS3012c: "that's just more a se a seasonal, a trend thing"; TS3012c: "shouldn't be too really too much shouldn't be too focussed on the covers")
- Button shape (round vs. square) was settled for the main keypad (square) but at least one member still personally preferred round, and it was waved off as "doesn't matter" rather than genuinely resolved.
